dishes.name: Mysore Pak
dishes.desc: A dense, ghee-heavy sweet made from gram flour, sugar and ghee, invented in the Mysuru palace kitchens.

dishes.name: Holige
dishes.desc: A stuffed sweet flatbread: chana dal and jaggery inside a thin dough, cooked on a tawa with ghee. Also called obbattu. Bhaskar's Mane Holige on D.V.G Road is a shop built around it.

dishes.name: Mysore Mutton Curry
dishes.desc: A dark, tangy mutton curry built on roasted spices rather than cream - popular in Singapore's Indian restaurants under this name, though food historians there dispute whether it has any real Mysuru origin at all. But still tasty to try

dishes.name: Bisi Bele Bath
dishes.desc: Literally "hot lentil rice" - a spiced, tangy rice-and-lentil dish and Karnataka's definitive comfort food.

dishes.name: Veg Palav
dishes.desc: Karnataka hotel-style vegetable rice, sona masuri and a green masala, sold as palav or rice bath. At Namma SLN it is the muddanna plate, ghee-heavy, vegetarian, on a banana leaf, next to the sabakki dose and idli.

dishes.name: Ragi Mudde
dishes.desc: Steamed finger-millet dumplings, torn by hand and dunked in saaru (thin lentil soup) - an old-Mysore rural staple.

dishes.name: Benne Masale Dosa
dishes.desc: A crisp dosa laced with butter (benne) and filled with spiced potato palya.

dishes.name: Davanagere Benne Dose
dishes.desc: A different animal from the Bengaluru version above - thicker and spongier, with puffed rice ground into the batter. First sold as a plain ragi dosa by a woman named Chennamma outside a Davanagere drama theatre in 1928; the buttery, puffed-rice version known today was developed later by her sons.

dishes.name: Khali Dose
dishes.desc: A plain, unstuffed dosa - thin, buttery, and a Bengaluru darshini specialty in its own right.

dishes.name: Donne Biryani
dishes.desc: Biryani made with short-grain jeerige sanna (seeraga samba) rice and a green masala base, served in a donne - a stitched areca-leaf cup.

dishes.name: Andhra Biryani
dishes.desc: Long-grain, chilli-forward biryani of the Andhra/Hyderabadi counter, not Karnataka donne. Meghana in Koramangala is the city's usual queue for the boneless chicken plate.

dishes.name: Kori Rotti
dishes.desc: A Tulu Nadu dish - spicy coconut-milk chicken curry poured over crisp, dry rice wafers.

dishes.name: Kori Gassi
dishes.desc: The chicken curry itself, without the wafers - a Mangalorean Bunt-community dish built on roasted coconut and dry red chilli. Kori is chicken, gassi is curry, in Tulu.

dishes.name: Neer Dosa
dishes.desc: A thin, lacy rice-batter crepe from the coast - the name literally means "water dosa."

dishes.name: Thatte Idli
dishes.desc: Plate-sized idli - thatte means plate - steamed wide and flat instead of in the usual small moulds, soft enough that it barely needs chewing.

dishes.name: Idli
dishes.desc: Steamed rice-and-urad cakes, the default Bengaluru breakfast with chutney. At Brahmins Coffee Bar they are one of four items on the board; New Modern Hotel puts a bucket of sambar on the table and lets you pour.

dishes.name: Maddur Vada
dishes.desc: A crisp, onion-forward vada from Maddur on the Bengaluru-Mysuru route, usually eaten hot with evening chai.

dishes.name: Rava Idli
dishes.desc: Semolina idli MTR made during the WWII rice shortage, when rava stood in for rice. Lalbagh Road is still the address for that plate.

dishes.name: Sabakki Dose
dishes.desc: A dosa with sabakki (sago) in the batter, crisp, often as masale dose. Namma SLN's Muddanna counters are the Bengaluru address people name for it.

dishes.name: Sabakki Idli
dishes.desc: Soft idli with sabakki mixed through, served with chutney and saagu. Same Muddanna kitchen as the sabakki dose and the veg pulav.

dishes.name: Bath Dose
dishes.desc: A dosa stuffed with veg pulav or rice bath, not potato palya. Namma SLN folds the muddanna rice into it; Umesh Dosa Point does a bath dosa with the same idea.

dishes.name: Mangalore Buns
dishes.desc: Slightly sweet, deep-fried banana buns from the coastal Udupi breakfast tradition.

dishes.name: Congress Kadlekai
dishes.desc: Spiced split peanuts from Iyengar bakeries, named after the 1969 Congress split. Best stuffed into a butter khara bun at the counter, not plated.

dishes.name: Cream Bun
dishes.desc: An Iyengar-bakery filled bun, closer to a doughnut with cream, coconut flakes, and tutti-frutti than to a Western cream bun. Thom's in Frazer Town is the city's usual reference.

dishes.name: Goli Baje
dishes.desc: Soft, tangy fritters from a fermented flour-and-curd batter - a Udupi teatime classic, best eaten hot.

dishes.name: Jolada Rotti
dishes.desc: A hand-flattened sorghum flatbread - the everyday bread of North Karnataka.

dishes.name: Akki Rotti
dishes.desc: A rice-flour flatbread patted straight onto a hot tawa by hand, not rolled, worked through with grated carrot, onion, coriander and green chilli.

dishes.name: Ragi Rotti
dishes.desc: The same hand-patted method as akki rotti, made with finger-millet flour instead of rice - denser, earthier, a staple alongside ragi mudde.

dishes.name: Yenne Badnekai
dishes.desc: Small eggplants stuffed with a peanut-sesame masala and slow-cooked in oil - a Dharwad-Hubballi classic.

dishes.name: Girmit
dishes.desc: Hubballi-Dharwad's answer to bhel - puffed rice tossed in a tangy onion-tomato-tamarind masala, sold at evening street stalls and eaten with mirchi bajji.

dishes.name: Kalaburgi Tahari
dishes.desc: North Karnataka's answer to biryani - mutton and rice cooked together in one pot, a Nizam-era dish still tied to a handful of old Kalaburgi eateries that only take cash.

dishes.name: Dharwad Peda
dishes.desc: A caramel-brown milk sweet with a history over 175 years old, still made at the original Babusingh Thakur shop on Dharwad's Line Bazaar - which the queues for it gave its name to.

dishes.name: Belagavi Kunda
dishes.desc: A soft, caramelised milk-and-khoa sweet from Belagavi - the story goes it was invented by accident when a confectioner let a pot of milk boil too long, though tellings disagree on who and when. The city is sometimes called Kundagiri after it.

dishes.name: Kesari Bath
dishes.desc: A bright orange semolina sweet, often plated next to khara bath as the combination "chow-chow bath."

dishes.name: Chow Chow Bath
dishes.desc: The two dishes above, served together on one plate with a spoon of coconut chutney between them - sweet kesari bath and spicy khara bath, a Bengaluru darshini staple with no single inventor on record.

dishes.name: Churmuri
dishes.desc: Puffed rice tossed with onion, tomato, chilli and a tangy dressing - Mysuru's answer to bhel puri.

dishes.name: Mylari Dosa
dishes.desc: A soft, thick, ghee-roasted dosa unique to a handful of Mysuru eateries - different in texture from a typical dosa.

dishes.name: Pandi Curry
dishes.desc: A dark, tangy Kodava pork curry, soured with kachampuli - a dark vinegar unique to Kodagu.

dishes.name: Kadambuttu
dishes.desc: Steamed rice dumplings from Kodagu, the traditional partner to pandi curry.

dishes.name: Filter Kaapi
dishes.desc: Traces back to the seven coffee beans the Sufi saint Baba Budan reportedly smuggled from Yemen to Chikmagalur in the 1670s - the slow-drip steel filter and the tumbler-davara pour came later, worked out in South Indian kitchens in the early 1900s. Strong decoction, hot milk, poured back and forth to cool and froth it. CTR and Vidyarthi Bhavan are two of Bengaluru's oldest addresses for it.

dishes.name: Majjige
dishes.desc: Spiced, thinned buttermilk - the everyday cooling drink that closes out a Karnataka meal.

dishes.name: Nannari Sherbet
dishes.desc: A deep red-brown cooling drink made from Indian sarsaparilla root syrup - a South Indian street-cart classic, best documented in Tamil Nadu and Kerala but popular in Mysuru too.

dishes.name: Kashaya
dishes.desc: A hot spiced herbal decoction from the Tulu Nadu coast, often the first thing offered to a guest.

dishes.name: Specialty Coffee
dishes.desc: Pour-over and single-origin, not tumbler-davara kaapi. Araku roasts beans from its own valley estates; Third Wave started roasting Chikmagalur lots out of Koramangala in 2016.

dishes.name: Craft Beer
dishes.desc: House pours from Bengaluru brewpubs, not a familiar bottle. Toit in Indiranagar opened the city's microbrewery habit in 2010; The Pump House did the same job for JP Nagar in 2018.

dishes.name: Death by Chocolate
dishes.desc: Corner House's piled ice-cream plate. The fudge is named Sheila's Fudge, after the family matriarch; the Residency Road shop opened in 1982.

dishes.name: Ice Cream Cake
dishes.desc: Lakeview Milk Bar's MG Road cake, from a parlour that started opposite Ulsoor Lake in 1930. Vanilla, chocolate, and raspberry were the original three flavours.

dishes.name: Tacos
dishes.desc: Chinita's order: tacos, then horchata, mole that is not mild-for-India. Indiranagar or Koramangala, same kitchen.

dishes.name: Tiramisu
dishes.desc: Chianti in Koramangala plates pasta, lasagna, then this. Order it after the meal, not as the reason to skip dinner.

dishes.name: Banoffee Pie
dishes.desc: Dyu Art Cafe's dessert people stay for: banana, toffee, cream, heavy sugar. Downstairs is for working; the pie is why the hours stretch.

dishes.name: Amrut Fusion
dishes.desc: Bengaluru-distilled single malt, launched internationally in 2009, aged faster in this heat. Drink it in the city; the Mysore Road tour is inconsistent, so call ahead.
